figure 15.1: FlashAttention: the same math, far less HBM traffic. Before (naive / SDPA), the interme­ diate attention matrix is materialized to HBM and re-read, so every query block re-streams the full  K/V row-block — many HBM round-trips. After (FlashAttention), the computation is tiled and fused  so each K/V tile is read into on-chip memory once for that tile and the result is accumulated in place —  far fewer HBM round-trips. The loop (probe → guardrails → metrics → green team) is  operational, but it needs decision gates to be actionable: (1) a release-blocking severity criterion  (e.g. any P0/P1 finding blocks promotion; P2/P3 are tracked but non-blocking); (2) test-corpus  ownership (a named team maintains the probe corpus and adds new cases from each red-team run);  (3) regression thresholds (a previously-passing probe that now fails is a regression and blocks  release).
